title: Adaptive prefetch & safe-rollback playbook for per-customer batching/caching
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers with heterogeneous traffic profiles need per-customer and per-route batching/caching policies to minimize per-token cost without risking regression to latency or output quality. Current manual tuning is slow, error-prone, and risky to apply globally. We need an adaptive recommendation system that generates safe config diffs (batch size, prefetch windows, prefix-cache allowlists/denylists, tier caps), validates them in shadow/canary, and supports automated rollback on SLO or quality regression.

This ticket scopes the prototype: a recommendation workflow that ingest route/customer telemetry, proposes candidate changes with risk scores, applies them behind a controlled rollout (shadow -> canary -> gradual), and provides automated rollback/revert triggers plus human approval gates for high-risk changes.
proposal:
Build a service (prefetch-advisor) that: 1) Profiles customers by latency distribution, prompt length distribution, and cache hit ratio; 2) Generates ranked recommendations (e.g., increase batch_size to N, enable prefix-KV prefetch TTL X, add route to strict-allowlist for cached prompts); 3) Attaches a risk score computed from tail-latency sensitivity, PSD (prompt similarity distance), and customer tier; 4) Outputs a safe diff combined with a rollout plan template that includes shadow testing and automated rollback triggers.

Key behaviors: recommendations are conservative by default (no more than +30% batch or +2x prefetch TTL), and aggressive suggestions require enterprise-tier or explicit allowlist. Allow/deny lists are enforced at apply-time to prevent dangerous cross-customer policies. The apply flow will create a change object in the config-store with metadata, linked PR, canary target, and metric watchers. A controller will execute the rollout and automatically revert if thresholds breach.

We will implement a minimal UI surface in Console to accept/reject suggestions and to inspect diffs before apply. The telemetry will be integrated with Console's per-route dashboards and Optimize's suggestions page.
acceptance_criteria: prefetch-advisor service can ingest 30 days of telemetry for a customer and produce at least three ranked policy proposals
Each proposal includes: policy diff (as text), estimated cost delta, estimated latency risk, risk_score, and required approval level
Apply flow: shadow apply (0% production impact) and canary apply to 1-5% traffic with metric watchers configured
Automatic rollback triggers: p95 latency increase > 20% or token cost increase > 15% or quality regression detected by canary eval harness
Console shows suggestion card with diff, risk score, and one-click request-approval or schedule-apply
Allowlist/denylist enforcement prevents aggressive changes for non-eligible customers (e.g., enterprise-only features gated behind tier)
Integration test that simulates a quality regression and verifies the controller reverts the change within 2 minutes
implementation_steps: Design data model for recommendations and safe-diff objects in config-store
Implement telemetry aggregator to compute per-customer distributions (prompt length, tokens per request, KV hit ratio, p50/p95/p99 latency)
Build recommendation generator that applies heuristics + simple ML scoring (logistic model) to rank candidates
Implement allowlist/denylist rules engine and tier checks; surface gating metadata in diff
Create rollout controller: supports shadow -> canary -> incremental -> full and automatic rollback hooks
Wire automatic metric watchers (latency, cost, error-rate) and quality eval harness for sampled canary outputs
Console integration: suggestion cards, diff viewer, approval flow + audit log entries
E2E tests: inject synthetic traffic, verify apply path, verify rollback on injected breach
Run pilot with 3 internal customers (platform, docs, and sample SaaS tenant) before broader rollout
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal pilot): run advisor in read-only mode and present suggestions to SRE/Platform UX. Phase 2 (shadow apply): enable shadow execution for low-risk proposals and collect metrics for 2 weeks. Phase 3 (canary): allow controlled canary for eligible enterprise tiers (1-5% traffic) with automated metric watchers. Phase 4 (gradual): expand to 25%/50%/100% with staggered windows and manual approvals for high-risk diffs. All phases record diffs and maintain audit trail for rollback. Any regression during canary triggers immediate automated revert and alerting to oncall.

High-risk changes (risk_score > 0.7) require two approvers and cannot be auto-applied.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring logic, risk computations, and allowlist enforcement
Integration tests for shadow and canary pipelines using replayed telemetry
Chaos tests: simulate GPU slowdowns and ensure rollback triggers based on latency SLOs
Quality regression test: use canned eval prompts and golden outputs; verify alarm fires when divergence exceeds threshold
Load test: simulate 10k RPS of typical PLG routes and observe batching efficiency and latency distribution
monitoring_and_recovery: Metric watchers will be configured per-change: p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost per 1k requests, error rate, KV cache hit ratio, and a quality regression score from eval harness. The rollout controller subscribes to these metrics and reverts changes when any configured threshold is crossed. Recovered state includes: automated revert change, generation of a rollback PR (if code/config changed), timeline in audit log, and automatic paging to oncall for P0-level breaches. Post-mortem workflow: automated incident stub created with attached change diff and snapshot of pre/post metrics.
